title: 12 Things Your Body Does That Sound Fake (But Are 100% True)
music_prompt: Instrumental cinematic documentary underscore, curious and mysterious, warm analog synth arpeggios, soft pulsing bass, light electronic percussion, gentle building tension, modern science-explainer vibe, 100 bpm
next_title: 12 Facts About Earth That Sound Fake

lines.t: Right now, as you watch this, your body is glowing.
Your stomach is trying to eat itself.
And your bones are being quietly dissolved... and rebuilt.
It sounds like science fiction. It's not. It's just a normal day inside you.
Here are twelve things your body does that sound completely fake, but are one hundred percent true.
And stay until number one, because it will change the way you see yourself in the mirror.
Number twelve. You are taller in the morning than you are at night.
Between the bones of your spine sit soft, gel-filled discs.
All day long, gravity squeezes them, and you shrink by about a centimeter.
When you lie down to sleep, the discs soak fluid back up, and you grow again.
Astronauts take this to the extreme. Without gravity, their spines stretch so much they can come home up to five centimeters taller... at least for a while.
Number eleven. Your stomach is constantly trying to digest itself.
Stomach acid is so strong it can corrode some metals.
So why doesn't it burn a hole straight through you?
Because your stomach is coated in a thick layer of protective mucus, and the cells underneath are replaced every few days.
You are basically growing a brand new stomach lining every week, just to stay one step ahead of your own acid.
Number ten. Your skeleton is being eaten alive. On purpose.
Inside your bones, cells called osteoclasts dissolve old bone, while osteoblasts build fresh bone in its place.
This never stops. Your body replaces roughly ten percent of your skeleton every single year.

stat: of your skeleton rebuilt every year

lines.t: Which means the skeleton you have today is not the one you had ten years ago.
Number nine. You glow in the dark.
In 2009, scientists in Japan used ultra-sensitive cameras to film people in total darkness.
And they discovered that the human body actually gives off visible light.
It comes from chemical reactions inside your cells. It's brightest around your face, and it peaks in the late afternoon.
So why have you never seen it? Because it's about a thousand times too weak for your eyes to detect.

sections.head: THERE'S A HOLE IN YOUR VISION

lines.t: Number eight. Right now, there is a hole in your vision, and your brain is hiding it from you.
Every eye has a blind spot, where the optic nerve connects to the back of the eye. There are no light sensors there at all.
So your brain simply paints over the gap with whatever it guesses should be there.
And it gets weirder. Every time your eyes jump from one point to another, your brain briefly blocks what you see, so you don't notice the blur.
Add it all up, and you spend a surprising part of every day effectively blind. And you never notice.

sections.head: THE MUSCLE YOU MIGHT NOT HAVE

lines.t: Number seven. Let's try something. Hold your palm up, touch your pinky to your thumb, and tilt your hand forward slightly.
Do you see a raised tendon running down the middle of your wrist?
That's the palmaris longus, a leftover muscle from our distant ancestors.
About fourteen percent of people don't have it at all, and they don't miss it.
It's so unnecessary that surgeons often borrow it to repair other parts of the body.
So, do you have it? Tell me in the comments.
Number six. You have a second brain, and it's in your gut.
Your digestive system is lined with around five hundred million neurons. That's more than your entire spinal cord.
It can run completely on its own, without any instructions from your brain.
And about ninety percent of your body's serotonin, a chemical tied to your mood, is made in your gut.

stat: of serotonin is made in your gut

lines.t: So when you feel butterflies in your stomach... that's not just a figure of speech.
And if you think that's strange, wait until you hear number three.

sections.head: YOUR BRAIN IS AN ENERGY HOG

lines.t: Number five. Your brain is the most expensive thing you own.
It makes up only about two percent of your body weight, but it burns around twenty percent of your energy.

stat: of your energy, from 2% of your weight

lines.t: Even when you're doing absolutely nothing, it runs on about twenty watts. Roughly the same as a dim light bulb.

stat: the power of a dim light bulb

lines.t: It's also the reason you can't tickle yourself. Your brain predicts your own touch, and cancels it out before you feel it.

sections.head: YOUR VEINS COULD CIRCLE THE EARTH

lines.t: Number four. If you laid every blood vessel in your body end to end, it would stretch about one hundred thousand kilometers.
That's enough to wrap around the Earth two and a half times.
And your heart pushes blood through all of it, beating about a hundred thousand times a day.
Over a lifetime, that's nearly three billion beats, without a single day off.
Number three. In the time it takes you to hear this sentence, your body will make around ten million new red blood cells.
That's more than two million every second, built deep inside the marrow of your bones.

stat: new red blood cells every second

lines.t: Each cell lives for about four months, racing around your body more than a hundred thousand times.
Then it's broken down, and its iron is recycled to build the next generation.

sections.head: YOUR DNA COULD REACH THE SUN

lines.t: Number two. Every cell in your body that has a nucleus holds about two meters of DNA.

stat: of DNA in a single cell

lines.t: All of it, folded into a space far smaller than the width of a hair.
Now multiply that by the trillions of cells that carry it.
Stretched end to end, the DNA in your body would reach the Sun and back... dozens of times.
And number one. You are almost entirely empty space.
Every atom in your body is a tiny nucleus surrounded by a vast emptiness.
If you squeezed the empty space out of every human on Earth, all eight billion of us would fit inside something the size of a sugar cube.
And those atoms? The calcium in your bones and the iron in your blood were forged inside ancient stars that exploded billions of years before Earth existed.
So the next time you look in the mirror, remember. You're not just looking at a person.
You're looking at stardust... that learned how to think.
If this blew your mind, wait until you see what's happening beneath your feet right now. That video is on your screen. I'll see you there.
